# Nobel Dahal

> Built Kaede, a cargo ERP for freight forwarders, end to end: IATA ONE Record and Cargo-XML messaging, AWB stock allocation under concurrency, carrier-portal automation, and a learning engine that suggests from an office's own history. Laravel contributor. Freelance full-stack developer (Laravel, Vue, PostgreSQL) in Kathmandu, Nepal. Contact: nobel@dahal.tech

## Case studies
- [Kaede](https://nobeldahal.com.np/work/kaede): The system a freight forwarder runs on. It reads the paperwork, learns how your office works, and talks to airlines, customers and drivers for you.
- [Kalimati Market](https://nobeldahal.com.np/work/kalimati): Nepal's largest wholesale produce market, run online. Daily prices for everyone, an ad-free Android app, and dues that traders pay from their phones through eSewa, Khalti or the bank.
- [GenericProperties](https://nobeldahal.com.np/work/generic-properties): Moved a US brokerage from Zoho to Microsoft Dynamics, then built what Dynamics was missing.

## Writing
- [What building IATA ONE Record taught me about linked data](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/what-one-record-taught-me): Air cargo is moving from messages to linked data. Lessons from serving ONE Record from a real cargo system, beyond what the spec tells you.
- [Handing out air waybill numbers without handing out the same one twice](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/handing-out-air-waybill-numbers): An air waybill number is a scarce, audited resource that two people will try to take at the same second. Check digits, stock states, and the locks that keep it honest.
- [mTLS and OAuth2 on the same call, step by step](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/mtls-and-oauth2-together): Some partner APIs want a client certificate on the connection and a bearer token on the request. Every way that goes wrong, in the order it went wrong for me.
- [Most waybills are the usual one](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/most-waybills-are-the-usual-one): 3,142 air waybills used just 149 routings, and five of them covered 87%. How that one number turned a data-entry form into a learning engine, without a model.
- [Designing a freight rate engine that four modes can share](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/designing-a-rate-engine): Air, sea, road and rail price freight in different units by different rules. How I built one engine for all four, and the rules that kept it correct.
- [Keeping PHPJasper alive for a cargo ERP](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/maintaining-phpjasper): Kaede prints air waybills, invoices and payslips through JasperReports. The PHP wrapper everyone uses had gone quiet, so I forked it and fixed what production kept finding.
- [Teaching a UI library to speak Nepali](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/teaching-a-ui-library-nepali): I translated Syncfusion's Essential JS 2, 64 components and over four thousand strings, into Nepali. These are the choices that made it read like Nepali and not like a dictionary.
- [Integrating eSewa and Khalti in Laravel without trusting the redirect](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/esewa-khalti-laravel): Most eSewa and Khalti tutorials stop when the success page loads. That's exactly where the fraud starts. A production pattern from a government payment page, for any Laravel app in Nepal.
- [Taking money on a government website](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/taking-money-on-a-government-website): How Kalimati's traders came to pay their dues from their phones through eSewa and Khalti, and the checks that keep a public payment page honest.
- [One developer, one market, no ads](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/one-developer-one-market): Building the website and Android app for Kalimati, the market that sets vegetable prices for half of Kathmandu, on my own.
- [A date that didn't fit in an integer](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/a-date-that-did-not-fit): The year 4123 crashed Laravel's date validation on 32-bit PHP. Here's how I found it, and the four-line fix that shipped in Laravel 8.
- [Finding the nearest agent among millions](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/finding-the-nearest-agent): A US brokerage moved from Zoho to Microsoft Dynamics. The data moved fine; the question it couldn't answer quickly was "who is closest to this lead?"
- [The check that only lived in the browser](https://nobeldahal.com.np/writing/the-check-that-only-lived-in-the-browser): How an email field in Everest Forms trusted the browser, how I closed it, and the regression I shipped and fixed along the way.
